speaker: ARCITE
text: Banished the kingdom? ’Tis a benefit,

speaker: ARCITE
text: A mercy I must thank ’em for; but banished

speaker: ARCITE
text: The free enjoying of that face I die for,

speaker: ARCITE
text: O, ’twas a studied punishment, a death

speaker: ARCITE
text: Beyond imagination—such a vengeance

speaker: ARCITE
text: That, were I old and wicked, all my sins

speaker: ARCITE
text: Could never pluck upon me. Palamon,

speaker: ARCITE
text: Thou hast the start now; thou shalt stay and see

speaker: ARCITE
text: Her bright eyes break each morning ’gainst thy

speaker: ARCITE
text: window

speaker: ARCITE
text: And let in life into thee; thou shalt feed

speaker: ARCITE
text: Upon the sweetness of a noble beauty

speaker: ARCITE
text: That nature ne’er exceeded nor ne’er shall.

speaker: ARCITE
text: Good gods, what happiness has Palamon!

speaker: ARCITE
text: Twenty to one he’ll come to speak to her,

speaker: ARCITE
text: And if she be as gentle as she’s fair,

speaker: ARCITE
text: I know she’s his. He has a tongue will tame

speaker: ARCITE
text: Tempests and make the wild rocks wanton.

speaker: ARCITE
text: Come what can come,

speaker: ARCITE
text: The worst is death. I will not leave the kingdom.

speaker: ARCITE
text: I know mine own is but a heap of ruins,

speaker: ARCITE
text: And no redress there. If I go, he has her.

speaker: ARCITE
text: I am resolved another shape shall make me

speaker: ARCITE
text: Or end my fortunes. Either way I am happy.

speaker: ARCITE
text: I’ll see her and be near her, or no more.

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: My masters, I’ll be there, that’s

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: certain.

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: And I’ll be there.

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: And I.

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Why, then, have with you, boys.

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: ’Tis but a chiding. Let the plough play today; I’ll

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: tickle ’t out of the jades’ tails tomorrow.

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: I am sure to have my wife as jealous

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: as a turkey, but that’s all one. I’ll go through;

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: let her mumble.

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: Clap her aboard tomorrow night

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: and stow her, and all’s made up again.

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: Ay, do but put a fescue in her fist

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: and you shall see her take a new lesson out and be

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: a good wench. Do we all hold against the Maying?

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Hold? What should ail us?

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: Arcas will be there.

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: And Sennois and Rycas; and

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: three better lads ne’er danced under green tree.

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: And you know what wenches, ha! But will the

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: dainty domine, the Schoolmaster, keep touch, do

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: you think? For he does all, you know.

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: He’ll eat a hornbook ere he fail.

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: Go to, the matter’s too far driven between him and

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: the tanner’s daughter to let slip now; and she must

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: see the Duke, and she must dance too.

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Shall we be lusty?

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: All the boys in Athens blow wind

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: i’ th’ breech on ’s. And here I’ll be and there I’ll be,

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: for our town, and here again, and there again. Ha,

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: boys, hey for the weavers!

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: This must be done i’ th’ woods.

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: O pardon me.

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: By any means; our thing of learning

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: says so—where he himself will edify the Duke

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: most parlously in our behalfs. He’s excellent i’ th’

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: woods; bring him to th’ plains, his learning makes

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: no cry.

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: We’ll see the sports, then every

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: man to ’s tackle. And, sweet companions, let’s rehearse,

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: by any means, before the ladies see us, and

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: do sweetly, and God knows what may come on ’t.

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Content. The sports once ended,

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: we’ll perform. Away, boys, and hold.

speaker: ARCITE
text: By your leaves, honest friends: pray you,

speaker: ARCITE
text: whither go you?

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Whither?

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Why, what a question’s that?

speaker: ARCITE
text: Yes, ’tis a question

speaker: ARCITE
text: To me that know not.

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: To the games, my friend.

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: Where were you bred, you know it not?

speaker: ARCITE
text: Not far, sir.

speaker: ARCITE
text: Are there such games today?

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: Yes, marry, are there,

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: And such as you never saw. The Duke himself

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: Will be in person there.

speaker: ARCITE
text: What pastimes are they?

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: Wrestling and running.—’Tis a pretty fellow.

speaker: THIRD COUNTRYMAN
text: Thou wilt not go along?

speaker: ARCITE
text: Not yet, sir.

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Well, sir,

speaker: FOURTH COUNTRYMAN
text: Take your own time.—Come, boys.

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: My mind misgives

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: me. This fellow has a vengeance trick o’ th’

speaker: FIRST COUNTRYMAN
text: hip. Mark how his body’s made for ’t.

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: I’ll be

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: hanged, though, if he dare venture. Hang him,

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: plum porridge! He wrestle? He roast eggs! Come,

speaker: SECOND COUNTRYMAN
text: let’s be gone, lads.

speaker: ARCITE
text: This is an offered opportunity

speaker: ARCITE
text: I durst not wish for. Well I could have wrestled—

speaker: ARCITE
text: The best men called it excellent—and run

speaker: ARCITE
text: Swifter than wind upon a field of corn,

speaker: ARCITE
text: Curling the wealthy ears, never flew. I’ll venture,

speaker: ARCITE
text: And in some poor disguise be there. Who knows

speaker: ARCITE
text: Whether my brows may not be girt with garlands,

speaker: ARCITE
text: And happiness prefer me to a place

speaker: ARCITE
text: Where I may ever dwell in sight of her?
